origins: Comparison with peers and social ideas of normal produce shame, especially for those with ongoing conditions. Longing to be “normal” can turn into grief or anger.
teaches: The psalmist says, “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” God told Samuel, “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Paul writes, “God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong” (1 Corinthians 1:27). Many of God’s servants in Scripture were far from ordinary. God does not call us to a statistical average. He calls us to be His beloved children. A good life is still possible.
self_statements: I will never be like them.
I cannot live a regular life.
errors: Believing people are either normal or not.
Predicting that I will never be okay.
Feeling different and concluding that I am abnormal.
questions: What does “normal” mean to me, and where did I get that idea?
Who do I know that is truly “normal”?
What has my difference taught me?
What does Scripture say about God choosing the weak and unusual?
What parts of a good life are available to me?
Who accepts me as I am?
truth: God does not measure me against a statistical average. He made me and loves me, and a good life is possible. My differences can be places where His grace shows.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
God chose the weak things of the world.
His power is perfected in weakness.
log: Each week, note one way you were accepted or lived well.
actions: Join a support group or friends.
Name something your experience taught you.
Say it when you feel different.
prayer: Lord, I long to be normal. Help me accept how You made me, find a good life, and show Your grace through my story. Amen.
